name: Project Kestrel
one_liner: A deep-learning network sensor that classifies every file and flow at wire speed and blocks unknown malware in under a second.

buyer.role: CISO or head of security operations
buyer.company_profile: Mid-size to large enterprises (1,000+ staff) in banking, insurance and state/local government that already run a firewall, sandbox and endpoint agent but still see malware slip through.

user: SOC analysts and network security engineers who triage detections and tune enforcement on firewalls, proxies and endpoints.

problem.summary: New malware variants appear faster than signature and sandbox pipelines can process them; sandboxes take minutes per sample and evasive samples detect them. By the time a verdict arrives the payload has spread. Security teams need a verdict at first encounter, on the wire, without baselining periods or tuning, and with enough context (family, kill-chain stage, infected hosts) to act immediately.

evidence.claim: Hundreds of thousands of new malware samples are registered every day, overwhelming signature-based approaches.
Sandboxes detonate samples in a restricted environment, which adds latency and can be evaded by environment-aware malware.
Network detection and response products inspect traffic to detect threats that endpoint tools miss.
Deep packet inspection allows examining full payloads in transit, a prerequisite for content-level classification on the network.

why_now.summary: Deep neural networks that read raw bytes now beat hand-engineered features on image and speech tasks, and cloud GPU training makes it affordable to retrain daily on fresh malware. Inference on commodity hardware is fast enough for sub-second verdicts.

features.feature: Passive network sensor (appliance or virtual) that reassembles files and flows and runs a proprietary neural network on raw bytes
features.why: Verdict at first encounter without waiting for detonation.

features.feature: Sub-second verdicts with threat family and indicators of compromise
features.why: Analysts need to know what it is, not just that it is bad.

features.feature: Automated enforcement via existing firewalls, web proxies and endpoint agents
features.why: Blocking without adding an inline box that could break traffic.
Helps when an attack is already in progress.

features.feature: SaaS management console with no baselining or tuning period
features.why: Shortens time to value versus anomaly-based tools.

out_of_scope: Full packet capture and forensics storage

competitors.name: FireEye network security (sandbox)
competitors.how_we_differ: We return verdicts in sub-seconds on the wire instead of minutes in a detonation chamber.

competitors.name: Darktrace
competitors.how_we_differ: No learning period: a pre-trained model classifies payloads, not deviations from a baseline.

competitors.name: Vectra
competitors.how_we_differ: We classify the malicious content itself rather than inferring attacker behaviour from metadata.

competitors.name: ExtraHop
competitors.how_we_differ: Focus on malware verdicts and prevention rather than network performance and visibility.

competitors.name: Suricata / Zeek with signature feeds (free)
competitors.how_we_differ: Detects unknown variants that have no signature yet.

differentiation: Pre-trained deep learning on raw bytes gives a verdict at first encounter, faster than sandboxes and without the weeks-long baselining of anomaly tools, while orchestrating blocks through controls the customer already owns. Usage-based pricing on traffic actually inspected lowers the up-front hardware commitment.

build.team: About 30 people: deep-learning researchers, threat researchers and network engineers, with founders from large-company ML security research
hardest_parts: Keeping false positives low enough to allow automated blocking
Retraining fast enough to keep up with drift in malware families
Proving efficacy against independent test sets buyers trust

pricing.model: SaaS subscription priced on traffic actually inspected; sensor hardware right-sized and bundled
pricing.entry_price: Working assumption: about $50,000/year for up to 1 Gbps inspected
pricing.rationale: Usage-based pricing reduces capex compared with appliance-plus-sandbox purchases and lets a buyer start on one segment.

comparables.price: No public list price at the time (quote-based enterprise sale)
No public list price at the time (quote-based enterprise sale)

go_to_market.first_customers: Ten security-forward mid-market firms (insurance brokers, regional banks, state agencies) with a small SOC and a recent malware incident, willing to run a passive proof of value on a SPAN port.
go_to_market.channel: Direct enterprise sales with proof-of-value deployments, then value-added resellers.
go_to_market.wedge: Passive deployment beside the existing sandbox to show what it missed, then turn on automated blocking.

risks: Buyers' scepticism of near-100% detection claims without independent tests
Incumbent firewall and endpoint vendors add ML detection to existing products
Long enterprise sales cycles for a new network sensor

riskiest_assumption.assumption: Security teams will pay a separate budget line for a network malware-verdict sensor next to their existing sandbox and endpoint tools.
riskiest_assumption.test: Run passive 2-week proof of value at 5 prospects on mirrored traffic and report detections their existing stack missed.
riskiest_assumption.success_signal: At least 3 of 5 prospects see confirmed misses by their current stack and request a purchase quote.

open_questions: How much traffic is encrypted at target customers?
Will buyers let a model block automatically?
Is the moat the model or the data pipeline?
